sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Turbine-Driven Critical Care Invasive Ventilators

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended — Chapter 5 on Sociétés à Responsabilité Limitée (Articles 710-1 et seq.)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL), Ministry of Justice
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation containing the articles of association, filed with RCSL and published in the electronic official collection (Mémorial C / Recueil électronique des sociétés)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for a SARL is €12,000 fully subscribed and paid in cash or in kind; funds must be held on a blocked capital-deposit account with a Luxembourg credit institution until RCSL registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the managing subscribers hereby constitute the société, accept the number of shares allotted to each as stated in the subscription table, and record payment of the minimum capital of €12,000. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at the address set forth in the articles and that the managing subscriber(s) may complete the legal formality regarding the occupation of the registered premises. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed sole manager of the company with the exclusive power to manage and represent the company in all acts, in accordance with the articles of association. RESOLVED, that the manager is authorised to dispatch all filings, sign all agreements, open bank accounts, and take any necessary measure for the incorporation and registration of the company, subject to law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of corporate name and preparation of draft articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) online name-reservation portal (MyLBR / lu.register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name-conflict search in the RCSL database; file an online reservation for the proposed legal entity name, which remains valid for a specified renewable period; submit the preliminary draft of the articles of association to the appointed notary for completeness review.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and legal form description
Identity details of each founding shareholder
Draft articles of association
Confirmation of name reservation issued by RCSL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused or queried, file a revised name or submit an administrative explanation with supporting documents; the RCSL allows repeated submission of alternative names within the same application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary appointed by the founders, acting under the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders appear before the notary to verify identity, legal capacity, contribution particulars and capital subscription. The notary reads, signs, and certifies the deed of incorporation containing the final articles, then delivers a certified copy for the subsequent registry filing.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national identity card of each founder
Proof of residential address of each founder
Certificate of RCSL name reservation
Final draft articles of association with share subscription table
Statement of contributions in cash or in kind and any valuation report required for non-cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect in the draft or legal capacity issue, execute a rectifying addendum before the same notary; no new reservation procedure is required unless the corporate name is affected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a blocked capital-deposit account and payment of the share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution licensed by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the bank with a certified draft of the notarial deed and complete KYC and AML documentation. Transfer or deposit the minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 into a blocked account in the name of the company 'in formation'. Obtain a bank certificate confirming the deposit and blockage.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the draft notarial deed
KYC / AML forms of all founders and ultimate beneficial owners
Valid photographic identification of all signatories
Bank references, source-of-funds evidence, and business activity description
Bank account application forms for the company in formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application for AML reasons, obtain a written explanation, adjust the ownership or funding documentation, and apply to a second Luxembourg credit institution; the notary may also use an independent attestation mechanism permitted by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation file with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) via electronic filing in MyLBR or at the RCSL counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original notarial deed, bank capital-deposit certificate, registered-office consent, and manager signature forms to the RCSL. Pay the registration fee and respond to any administrative requests. The RCSL reviews legal conformity and registers the company in the commercial and companies register.
required_dossiers: Original notarial deed of incorporation
Bank certificate evidencing payment and blocking of EUR 12,000 minimum capital
Sworn statement of identity and capacity of the elected manager(s)
Consent of the owner of the registered office address
RCSL registration application form and statutory declaration of compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a query from the RCSL, submit a corrective memorandum and any missing documents within the deadline indicated in the electronic notice; if the application is formally refused, the founders may appeal to the Luxembourg District Court within two months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of incorporation extracts and issuance of the registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL and the Luxembourg electronic official gazette (Mémorial C / Recueil électronique des sociétés)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCSL registration, the registry automatically prepares and publishes required extracts on the electronic official collection. The company may then download its certificate of registration (extrait des informations), open final bank accounts, and proceed with VAT and social security registrations.
required_dossiers: RCSL registration acknowledgment reference
Certified copy of the notarial incorporation deed
Identity details of all directors and shareholders
Confirmed registered-office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains an error, file a request with the RCSL for correction of the official record; if publication has not occurred within the statutory timeframes, re-apply with a service-request evidence and escalate to the RCSL supervision unit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Directorate General for Industry) for the industrial establishment permit; Ministry of Health — Directorate of Health for medical-device manufacturing activities; Administration de l'environnement for environmental permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (industrial establishment permit) and Luxembourg medical-device manufacturer registration / EUDAMED establishment registration for the manufacture of invasive critical-care ventilators

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement — Environmental Protection Agency (Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 2 — EIA screening notice only; not subject to full EIA report because ventilator assembly is considered a low-volume mechanical/electronic manufacturing operation under the Luxembourg Act of 13 May 2008 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge threshold of 50 m³/day for sanitary and cleaning effluents; VOC / solvent-release limit below 0.5 tonnes per year; waste-classification and handling per Regulation (EU) 1357/2014 and national waste legislation; mandatory municipal and hazardous waste collection contracts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from the competent commune with expert review by the Luxembourg fire and rescue service (CGDIS) covering escape routes, extinguishing systems and hazardous-materials storage; structural-load inspection certificate issued by a registered building engineer; and occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including electrical equipment compliance and workplace ventilation standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) / Luxembourg Inland Revenue, online portal: Guichet.lu and MyGuichet.lu; VAT matters administered by Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing a Luxembourg SARL must complete notarized incorporation before the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL), file with the Registration Department (AEDT) for VAT purposes on form 1027, and obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number (Numéro d'identification à la TVA) and a national business number (n° matricule). Registration must occur prior to commencing taxable activities; non-established taxpayers may require a Luxembourg tax representative for VAT compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg applies a classical corporation tax system with no check-the-box pass-through election for SARLs; SARL is subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune). No hybrid mismatch election is available for SARL classification under domestic law; hybrid mismatch outcomes are addressed via ATAD-aligned rules and OECD BEPS Action 2 domestic provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual taxable turnover threshold for mandatory VAT registration; registration mandatory for any taxable person established or whose permanent establishment in Luxembourg carries out taxable transactions, subject to small business exemption rules, and compulsory for foreign suppliers of distance sales exceeding EUR 10,000 or any B2C electronic services under the EU One-Stop-Shop regime)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: E-invoicing is not mandatory for domestic B2B transactions; Luxembourg mandates the issuance of structured electronic invoices for B2G contracts (PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format) from 2023. No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping (such as SAF-T continuous transaction controls) is required at national level; VAT returns must be filed electronically via eCDF平台 (MyGuichet.lu) on a monthly, quarterly, or annual basis, with EC Sales Lists and Intrastat filings as applicable for cross-border transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf (Article 44 of the Luxembourg VAT Law). The exporter must hold proof of export and evidence that the goods physically left the EU within the statutory period (generally 90 days from supply, extendable to 180 days). Services related to exported goods (incoterms DDP handling, transport, ancillary services) may qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is established outside the EU and the service is directly linked to the exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (single administrative document or electronic customs declaration summary declaration export under EU UCC)
Commercial invoice and proof of contract
Bill of Lading or airway bill with carrier's dated receipt
Inward Remittance Certificate (evidence of foreign exchange repatriation from overseas buyer)
Cargo movement evidence (transit/pre-consignment records, logbook, GPS trace) where automated controls have been de-authorized
Export declaration acceptance acknowledgment (LR/IE-599 electronic acknowledgment)
Proof of physical exit (certificate of arrival or customs stamp from destination country when available)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may disallow zero-rating and retroactively invoice VAT at 17% (or applicable rate) plus late interest and penalties up to 10% of the tax due per month of delay (maximum 50%), and may apply fines up to EUR 250,000 for serious export-fraud cases. Fraudulent zero-rating schemes trigger criminal sanctions, imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years, and joint and several liability for directors. Export documentation must be retained for at least 10 years; failure to substantiate exports results in VAT clawback, interest at 0.8% per month (statutory rate), and disqualification from refund claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as national central bank and member of the Eurosystem; foreign exchange administration operates under EU capital movement liberalisation, with CSSF supervising financial markets and money laundering controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls for residents or non-residents on capital or current account transactions under the EU Treaty and consolidated capital movement rules. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, royalty, and interest repatriation are free of foreign exchange approvals, subject only to corporate governance, anti-money laundering, and tax compliance (including withholding tax). The EUR is a fully convertible currency; cross-border settlement in EUR or foreign currency is unrestricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export contract proceeds may be held in foreign currency accounts with Luxembourg banks; only statistical reporting obligations under BCL balance-of-payments rules apply for transactions exceeding EUR 12,500 or specified monthly thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low to medium for offshore digital electronic money institutions. Luxembourg entities may hold e-money accounts with CSSF-authorised EMIs, but an offshore EMI not passporting under PSD2 into Luxembourg cannot offer regulated payment services to a Luxembourg-domiciled company; the entity would face restrictions on receiving client funds, LC issuance, and high-value treasury transactions. Such EMIs are better suited as auxiliary payment accounts, not as primary clearing rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated SARL with non-resident ownership, Luxembourg AML/KYC rules impose an in-person interview and physical document verification for at least first-time signatories and Ultimate Beneficial Owners. Remote notarisation and video identification may be accepted by certain banks if using certified EU eIDAS e-signatures, but most tier-1 banks require an initial physical meeting at the relationship manager's office or at a Luxembourg notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border ownership with ultimate beneficial owner in a non-EEA tax haven or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised corporate charters, current extract of Luxembourg trade register, apostilled passport copies, bank reference letters, detailed source-of-wealth statements, group structure chart, evidence of commercial substance (office lease, local payroll, telephone/fax), and recent audited financial statements of parent entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-value wire flows from government buyers and procurement ministries for life-support medical devices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed supply contracts or framework agreements, EU CE marking certificate, ISO 13485 certificate, proforma invoices, end-customer due diligence file for counterparties, sanctions screening report, and procurement tender documentation explaining the nature of fund flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of third-party payment agents or distribution intermediaries for export deals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly notarised agency and distribution agreements, KYC file on each agent including beneficial ownership, copies of agent licences, commission schedules, and a description of how agent commissions are calculated and settled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid movement of capital injection from a non-banking corporate loan rather than equity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Loan agreement, board resolutions approving the loan, proof of source of lender funds, financial statements, and an explanation of the commercial rationale for debt rather than equity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing uses SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA transfers or SEPA Instant/TARGET2 for EUR transfers from EEA countries. For capital contributions, the remitting bank must apply Luxembourg BCL purpose code '2061' (investment in capital) or '2065' (capital increase) on the payment instruction; the receiving bank will require a copy of the notarised capital increase resolution, proof of UBO identity, and declaration of source of funds for the SARL's capital account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail for commercial settlement is SWIFT MT103 for direct payments, complemented by bank-to-bank reimbursements under documentary collections. For government buyers, the preferred rail is an irrevocable LC confirmed by a Luxembourg bank pursuant to UCP600, with usance exposure financed via supplier loans or LCs discounted at the bank; SEPA CT transfers are used for EU-based suppliers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forwards with tenors aligned to the ventilators' order-to-cash cycle
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for hedging currencies where Luxembourg banks cannot trade deliverable forwards (e.g., CNY or INR counterparty restrictions)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (e.g., EUR/USD) when the SARL has matching long-term export receivables in USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels): balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, annex, statutory auditor's report (if triggered), and management report (if mandatory)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting within 6 months of financial year-end; deposit with RCS within 7 months of balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Manager/director fines of EUR 750-25,000; court coercive penalty orders; after three consecutive unfiled years plus formal notice, RCS administrative strike-off and loss of legal capacity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax 17%, solidarity surcharge 7% of IRC, and municipal business tax ~6.75% for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), investment tax credit (8% for eligible investments), R&D incentives, participation exemption for dividends and capital gains (100% exemption under conditions).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1000 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via the Luxembourg e-filing portal (eCDF)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 6 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., for a calendar year ending 31 December, due by 30 June of the following year). Extensions may be granted upon justified request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification (name, address, registration number, tax ID)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide local tax representative details if non-resident; ensure valid Luxembourg tax number.
Report Luxembourg-source income only; apply DTA provisions if applicable.
Only expenses directly related to Luxembourg-source income are deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (foreign tax credit, investment tax credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty relief via Form 105 and attach TRC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of the tax due (minimum EUR 250). Interest accrues at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax. Additional fines for incomplete or false declarations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1001 (Municipal Business Tax Return) filed via the same eCDF portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same deadline as Form 1000 (6 months after fiscal year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable basis (trade income as per corporate income tax return)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to the PE based on arm's length principles.
Use the rate of the commune where the PE is located.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Same penalty structure as Form 1000: 10% late filing penalty, monthly interest, and additional fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if the parent holds at least 10% of the share capital for 12 months; treaty rates may also apply)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the beneficial owner must submit a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) and a Form 105 (or equivalent) to the Luxembourg tax authorities. The payer must apply the reduced rate at source if the conditions are met; otherwise, a refund claim can be filed within the statutory period (usually 5 years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive for EU affiliates; treaty rates may apply (e.g., 5% or 10%). Interest: generally 0% withholding tax, but a 15% rate applies to excessive interest or payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if the group turnover exceeds EUR 50 million and related-party transactions exceed EUR 1 million (goods) or EUR 500,000 (services). Master File required if group turnover exceeds EUR 50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for entities engaged in IP holding, financing, and other mobile activities. Manufacturing entities (e.g., medical device production) are expected to have substantial substance, including physical premises, qualified employees, and core decision-making functions in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of taxable income, falsification of books, or concealment of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to 100% of the tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years, and mandatory publication of the judgment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they participated in or knowingly allowed the evasion. Civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment are possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox company with no real business activity, no employees, or no physical presence in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits, recharacterization of income, imposition of penalties up to 10% of the adjusted income, and potential nullification of tax rulings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if the corporate veil is pierced due to fraudulent or abusive conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement anti-money laundering procedures, conducting transactions with sanctioned entities, or facilitating money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 5 million for legal entities, imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals, and revocation of business licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal liability, including imprisonment, if they knowingly participate in or fail to prevent AML breaches. Travel bans and asset freezes may also apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain transfer pricing documentation, applying non-arm's length pricing, or ignoring TP adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties up to 10% of the adjusted amount, and interest on underpaid tax. In severe cases, criminal charges for tax evasion may be pursued.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they approved or ignored non-compliant TP policies, especially in cases of gross negligence.
